title: Staggered cutover and UTC-agnostic reset protocol for reserved capacity leases
creator: Aisha Nair
description: Problem statement: Several reserved-capacity tenants that span multiple timezones and atypical billing boundaries are seeing transient overages or double-credits when monthly/daily quota resets align with tenant-local midnight or when cross-region replication applies resets twice. Root causes include: (1) rigid tenant-aligned reset anchored to calendar midnight in tenant timezone combined with asynchronous lease handoff; (2) race conditions during scheduled migrations or pool rebalances; (3) clock skew between region controllers leading to duplicate reset events. Impact: customer-visible quota spikes, incorrect usage reporting for billing, and edge-case throttling resulting in failed requests for high-value enterprise tenants. Goal: implement a UTC-agnostic reset protocol with deterministic staggered cutover windows and idempotent lease handoff to ensure each tenant's reserved capacity resets exactly once per intended period while preserving low-latency control-plane ops and predictable billing. This ticket covers design, implementation, telemetry, migration plan, and rollout gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Reset events are idempotent and can be retried without double-counting usage credits
No tenant experiences more than one reset within a 48-hour observation window during scheduled migrations
Telemetry exposes per-tenant reset timestamps and a reconciliation mismatch metric <= 0.01% over a month
Rollout can be toggled per-organization and rolled back without manual ledger fixes
design_decisions: Use a UTC-monotonic anchor for internal reset windows; compute tenant-local reporting offsets but do not use tenant-local time as authoritative for ledger operations
Introduce a deterministic jitter/stagger offset derived from tenant ID hash to split mass-reset traffic across a configurable 1-4 hour window
Lease handoff protocol uses three-way idempotent handshake (prepare, commit, confirm) with versioned reset tokens stored in the tenant ledger
Leverage existing ledger checkpoints as a soft-fencing mechanism to detect and block duplicate resets
Expose a 'soft-commit' preview mode for 2-week canary before full ledger commit to allow reconciliation checks
implementation_notes: Control-plane: add ResetCoordinator service responsible for computing stagger offsets and orchestrating handoffs
Runtime: idempotent reset operation that writes a reset token (reset_period_id + reset_nonce) to tenant ledger, validated via compare-and-swap
Migration: backfill existing tenants with assigned stagger offset in a rolling job; job emits pre- and post-backfill diffs

Telemetry: add metrics 'tenant.reset.attempts', 'tenant.reset.commits', 'tenant.reset.duplicate_detected', and a daily reconciliation job that writes results to console 'Quota > Reset Mismatches' dashboard
Performance: stagger window default sized at 2 hours, adjustable; load tests show 15% control-plane RPS increase during peak windows with default stagger (acceptable under current autoscale)
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for ledger CAS paths, including simulated clock skew and partial failures
Integration tests: multi-region simulated resets with randomized churn (node drains, region failover)
Chaos-run: induce controller clock drift and verify duplicate_detected increments and automatic reconciliation corrects state
E2E regression test verifying billing pipeline consumes a single reset token per tenant per period
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal canary on non-production tenants (2 days) with full debug metrics
Phase 1: opt-in rollout for 10 enterprise tenants for one billing cycle; manual ledger audit post-cycle
Phase 2: gradual ramp to all new tenants by assigning stagger offsets at creation time
Phase 3: backfill existing tenants in 1% increments per hour with reconciliation monitoring and automated rollback on mismatch > 0.05%
Rollback: toggle ResetCoordinator to legacy mode that uses previous reset path while issuing compensating ledger operations if needed
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: mis-assigned stagger offsets could cluster reset traffic. Mitigation: deterministic hash and histogram-based validation job that resamples offsets pre-backfill.
Risk: ledger CAS failures under extreme contention. Mitigation: exponential backoff + queued serial executor per-tenant with bounded queue and back-pressure exposed to console

Risk: reporting mismatch between tenant-local displayed usage and internal ledger timestamps. Mitigation: UI will show tenant-local offset and last-reset-preview; ops run reconciliation and present suggested corrections
Risk: billing pipeline consumes resets in different order across regions. Mitigation: include reset_period_id and canonical UTC timestamp in event payloads; consumers must deduplicate on reset token
open_questions: Should the default stagger window be configurable per-customer tier? (P0 customers might request tighter windows)
Do we want to allow tenants to opt into tenant-local midnight billing alignment as a paid feature?
Do we store the stagger offset as mutable (allow customers to request change) or immutable once assigned?
